title: Process and Dynamic Assembly Execution
platform_conditions: .NET Framework 4.x and modern .NET (UseShellExecute semantics differ: shell-resolved on Windows when true, exec-family style when false)
security_mechanism: Process.Start with UseShellExecute=true hands the arguments to the OS shell (cmd.exe / Explorer), so metacharacters and additional commands inside an interpolated argument are executed by the shell rather than passed as data to the target program; even with UseShellExecute=false an argument beginning with '-' becomes an option of the spawned tool. The dynamic-execution family has a second axis: Assembly.Load and Type.GetType(name) followed by reflection (Activator.CreateInstance, MethodInfo.Invoke) turn an attacker-supplied type or assembly name into arbitrary object construction and method invocation inside the process.

source_sink_clues.source: Request fields used as command arguments, tool names, file paths passed to helper executables, and attacker-influenced type/assembly names resolved via reflection or plugin loading.
source_sink_clues.sink: Process.Start(ProcessStartInfo with UseShellExecute=true) or interpolated arguments; Assembly.Load / Assembly.LoadFrom with dynamic names; Type.GetType plus Activator.CreateInstance / MethodInfo.Invoke

tracking_guards: Require a fixed executable path with UseShellExecute=false and each dynamic value as a separate element of ArgumentList; verify values that could start with '-' are passed after '--' or rejected; for reflection, require an allowlist of type/assembly names resolved from a fixed mapping instead of from input.
not_candidate_when: The executable path is constant, UseShellExecute is false, and dynamic values travel as single ArgumentList elements to a tool with no option parsing; reflection targets come from a compiled-in allowlist; or the argument is validated against a strict grammar that cannot introduce shell syntax or option characters.
public_references: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html
CWE-470: Use of Externally-Controlled Input to Select Classes or Code — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/470.html
